summary:
THE HEADLINE: h_docs' TWO NAMED ITEMS AND EVERY REPAIR THEY MADE HOLD UP UNDER RE-MEASUREMENT, AND THE ROUND'S PATTERN REPEATED ANYWAY -- I FOUND THREE DEFECTS IN docs/04_CONTRACT.md THAT NOBODY FILED, AND THE SHARPEST TWO ARE BOTH THE 'FIX INTRODUCED THE NEXT DEFECT' SHAPE THE BRIEF WARNS ABOUT.

(1) THE RETIRED SELF-CONTRADICTING SENTENCE SURVIVES IN THIS DOCUMENT, WHICH IS NOW THE TREE'S LAST PRESENT-TENSE CARRIER OF IT. d57bdc0's headline repair was h_cap rewriting cap.clamp's UNREACHABLE arm because 'no lift can be earned at all' contradicted itself. docs/04_CONTRACT.md:638 -- h_docs' file, in the D16 paragraph h_docs edited eighteen lines above -- still defines that gate's UNREACHABLE reading as '(no lift can be earned at all)'. I reached the arm on a live build: at CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=1000 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 the gate is reachable=False and its own clause reads 'the cap of 1000 is below its hard ceiling of 4096, so lifts ARE earned here'. _clamp_gate's docstring says in as many words 'THIS IS NOT "no lift can be earned"'. In src/ the string now occurs only inside three past-tense retractions; the document is the only place it is still asserted as what the gate means.

(2) THE ONE CLAUSE h_docs REWROTE IN THE D16 PARAGRAPH REPLACED A TRUE SENTENCE WITH A FALSE ONE, AND IT IS A CHECKER'S CAUSAL CLAIM ADOPTED WITHOUT MEASURING IT. The old text said the lowering the `max` guards against is 'reachable at CAP_FAB_START=5000 against FAB_SLOTS=4096' -- true. g_docs finding[8] said 'The STATE is reachable ... but the CALL is not', and h_docs put that into the document verbatim as a headline. I instrumented _clamped_lift and built: at CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=5000 new_valve makes exactly that call -- _clamped_lift(5000, 4096, 0.08, 8) -- from _one_lift, BEFORE _one_lift tests c >= hard. The call is not merely reachable, it EXECUTES on an ordinary environment setting, and _clamped_lift's own docstring lists 'EVERY EXECUTING CALLER IS INSIDE new_valve -- _lift_moves, _one_lift, and the mask-and-inert test'. The document now contradicts the file it is summarising, in the paragraph whose whole subject is not overstating reachability.

(3) THE LINE-CITATION CLASS h_docs FOUND AND FIXED FIVE TIMES AT :69-71 IS STILL LIVE 60 TIMES IN THE SAME FILE, AND ONE OF THOSE SITES CONTRADICTS ITSELF. docs/04_CONTRACT.md:1478-1481 offers three `path:NNN` citations as 'the proof ... with no counter-example' that ISSUES.md line citations drifted by +88. All three miss: M38 is at capacity/levers.py:474 not :346, M36 at :491 not :363, and M23's companion figure 'ISSUES.md:357' is not in tok/levers.py at all -- it was deleted at 0e056e7, whose subject line is 'Citations name symbols now'. Two sentences later the same paragraph says the class was 'Repaired in src/data/ and src/tok/ only', i.e. the paragraph names as live evidence a citation it then says was converted away. h_docs' own +13-line insertion into tok/levers.py and h_cap's +13 into capacity/levers.py moved two of the three further off in this very commit.

WHAT I COULD NOT BREAK, AND I TRIED. THE CAP REWRITE IS THE REAL THING. I wrote my own sweep without looking at theirs and the algebra holds everywhere I can reach it: 'a lift lowers a cap exactly when int(CAP_LIFT_MIN) < 0 AND int(CAP_LIFT x cap) < 0' gives 0 mismatches over 238,095 cells of my grid; 'int(frac*cap) <= floor' 0 of 56,166; 'int(frac*cap) >= 0' 0 of 62,678; 0 counterexamples to either identity at cap >= 0; 0 lowerings anywhere with floor >= 0. Every one of the twelve `lift_to(a,b,c) = d` claims in the document re-evaluates correctly against src/spine/derive.py, and so do all 16 in capacity/api.py and 8 in capacity/levers.py. Their correction of g_docs' boundary is right: identity 2 first breaks at cap = -13, not -12. And the reachability is real -- build({'CAP_TARGETS':'experts', 'CAP_FAB_START':'-5'}) then new_valve gives cap_experts = -5 with origin ('operator (fab_start=-5)', 'sentinel 0 -> hard ceiling 4096'), and both identities hold there, so the sentence that called that regime empty really was refuted at its own named cap. NOTHING WAS NARROWED AND NOTHING WAS REMOVED: the refusal, the guard and all three Gates are byte-identical, no check was touched, no wire was spent (C4 still prints 23 couplings / 19 wires of 25 / 4 intra-package), and K13's 77 claims and the eight live counts are unmoved.

Q-OPT-2 IS CORRECT DOWN TO THE OLD TREE. .rework/oracle/ is eight files and the 575 replayed cases are exactly 60+36+7+216+105+7+112+32 of those eight, none of them this function. I checked the impossibility claim against aee4a52:self_organize.py myself rather than relaying it: 48 module-level functions, none converting windows to steps; _lr_total is a nested def inside main() at line 6367; `BATCH_W * ACCUM` occurs 0 times in the 9,859 lines. capture_oracle.lift() really does only take module-level FunctionDefs. And tests/test_derive.py::smoke really does carry the hand-derived block. THE D17 REWRITE IS ALSO A REAL REPAIR: .rework/DECISIONS.md:445-448 says the second sentence 'means the refusal must be turn-off-able WITHOUT EDITING CODE' and :468-470 that 'the switch exists so that revisiting it costs an environment variable rather than a commit' -- the old paraphrase ('not a revert') was the softening h_docs says it was, ckpt/api.py states the cost plainly, and the constant is spelled in exactly five files.

THE O13 PROPOSAL IS ALMOST RIGHT AND HAS ONE NARROWING INSIDE IT. I implemented their four widenings from their own words, without their driver: examined 3 -> 6, findings 0 -> 3, all three the same true defect (spine/assemble.py once, docs/03_WIRING.md twice), no false positive -- exactly as claimed. But the set is NOT a superset: requiring the gap to END in an attribution verb drops src/fabric/api.py's citation of spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_windows, which O13 examines TODAY through a bare ': ' gap (the shipped _O13_GAP makes the verb OPTIONAL). Their rule silently retires a live detection. Accepting either form -- `VERB_END.search(gap) or (_O13_GAP.match(gap) and re.search(r'[A-Za-z:]', gap))` -- gives 7 examined, the same 3 findings, still no false positive. Filed with the one-line fix. Their population numbers are also one off mine in two places: I count 91 nearby-quotation citations and 72 gap-drops where they report 90 and 71; the 15 <module> drops, the 1 short drop and the 3 examined match exactly, and O13's own printed '723 citation(s) opened ... 3 of those attribute a quoted sentence' matches their after-number.

THE SUITE AND THE BASELINE. Green on every leg: ownership 13+33, contract 15+66, census 8, assemble 9, couplings 4, fabric 8, derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches. h_docs' one red leg was REAL and was CORRECTLY RED -- K15 catching a live false-equation in src/opt/api.py:1930, a file outside their ownership line -- and the supervisor applied the one-string repair in d57bdc0 (`OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0` becomes the f-string `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM={shift_warm}`). I re-read the repaired branch and it interpolates the value on a branch admitting `shift_warm <= 0`, which is the right fix and not a narrowing. The brief's baseline numbers (contract 15+59, ownership 13+32) are simply older than the siblings' self-test additions; nothing regressed.
